To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Rj2 is a soybean R gene controlling nodulation with specific Bradyrhizobial strains and that Rj2 encodes a member of the TIR-NBS-LRB class of plant R proteins.
Rj2 is allelic to Rfg1 and encodes a TIR-NBS-LR protein that confers genotype-specific nodulation restriction in soybean.
the host specificity in the soybean–Bradyrhizobium symbiosis is controlled by the soybean Rj2 and Sinorhizzobium fredii Rfg1 genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and biochemical basis of the legume– rhizobia symbiosis, and how it has evolved to become one of the most successful mutualistic associations in the plant kingdom.
the molecular basis of the legume–bacteria symbiosis, which is a model system for studying the evolution of host–pathogen interactions.
the molecular basis of legume-rhizobia symbiosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the symbiosis is a complex process, which is controlled by both host and bacterial genes.

the symbiotic relationship is a result of a balance between the ability of rhizobia to evade the immune responses of the host and the ability of the host to detect and respond to these evasion mechanisms.

the Rj2 and the Rfg1 genes encode host resistance genes that restrict infection and nodulation with specific bacterial strains, and the corresponding bacterial genes encode avirulence genes required for infection and nodulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified the R genes that control the host specificity of the symbiosis.
R gene controlled host specificity is determined through recognition of rhizobial effector proteins by the host R proteins.
the symbiotic interaction between soybean and rhizobia involves a common mechanism of plant immunity, which has evolved to prevent infection by pathogenic bacteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rhizobia have evolved mechanisms to overcome the plant immune system in order to establish the symbiosis, and that the host R genes have co-evolved to recognize these rhizobial factors.
rhizobia have to be able to evade the plant immune system, which is normally triggered by the presence of rhizobial effector proteins.
the host specificity of rhizobia is determined by specific bacterial factors that are recognized by the plant immune system.
